state.case_summary:
A 25-year-old woman presented with a painless lump in the left cheek, first noted nine months earlier. She reported no toothache, numbness, or systemic symptoms and had no significant medical history. On examination, there was left facial asymmetry without skin changes. Palpation revealed a firm, mobile, non-tender mass approximately 4 cm in diameter, located deep in the left buccal space and extending below the zygomatic arch; no cervical lymphadenopathy was noted. Intraorally, there was a bulge of the left buccal mucosa; palpation confirmed a well-defined, firm, non-tender mass.

An orthopantomogram showed no bony destruction of the mandible or maxilla, with only a healed post-extraction socket in the region of tooth 36. Ultrasonography of the left cheek demonstrated a discrete, well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass measuring 2.6 × 2.0 cm, overlying the parotid gland, with no increase in internal vascular flow or calcification. Contrast-enhanced CT of the head and neck revealed a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor measuring 2.7 × 3.7 × 4.0 cm in the left buccal space, indenting but not destroying adjacent bones (including the posterior maxillary sinus wall, medial pterygoid, masseter, and temporal muscle), and extending into the temporal space; the mass was supplied by branches of the left buccal artery.

Fine-needle aspiration biopsy yielded a hypocellular sample with erythrocytes, histiocytes, and neutrophils but showed “no signs of malignancy.” An intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated “wide fibroblast proliferation, extremely similar to a fibroma.”

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Solitary fibrous tumour
B. Lipoma
C. Pleomorphic adenoma
D. Schwannoma
E. Fibrous histiocytoma
F. Benign glandular tumor
G. Dermoid cyst
H. Malignant tumor
